newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering gradually - EPA report.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering gradually - EPA report.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to improve and private demand is firm, although the pace of recovery is gradual, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its latest monthly report on Tuesday.
The closely watched wording of the EPA's monthly economic assessment has been unchanged since November last year.
The report said consumption was gradually recovering, housing construction levels were still at high levels and industrial production was on a rising trend.
A fall-off in consumer spending after Japan's sales tax rose to five percent from three percent in April is expected to have run its course by the end of June, an EPA official said.

On housing, demand for privately owned homes has fallen steeply after the tax rise and could be expected to fall further, he said. But he added that demand for rental housing had nearly hit bottom, while the decline in demand for other types of housing had been comparatively modest.
"It is difficult to forecast a trend for housing. We need to watch these (indicators) a little longer," he said.
The official also said export volumes were high, while growth in import volumes was limited, adding that this trend should continue in the near term.

"Export volumes increased dramatically as manufacturers shifted the focus to overseas demand after the rise in the sales tax, and there are few factors working to increase imports at the moment," he said.
But he said that in the long term, structural changes such as the shift of factories overseas meant Japanese firms were unlikely to embark on an ever-increasing export drive.
He added that even in the medium term, high capacity utilisation rates would likely cap exports from domestic factories as firms were more likely to increase exports from plants abroad.
